name: RetICL / Learning to Retrieve Iteratively for In-Context Learning (a.k.a. IterR / iterative retrieval)
venue: EMNLP 2024 (Main Conference, pages 7156-7168); Outstanding Paper. Also arXiv:2406.14739.
authors_affiliation: Yunmo Chen (Johns Hopkins University; work done while interning at Microsoft), Tongfei Chen, Harsh Jhamtani, Patrick Xia, Richard Shin (Google; while at Microsoft), Jason Eisner, Benjamin Van Durme. Primary affiliation: Microsoft (Microsoft Semantic Machines), with Johns Hopkins University.
code_url: N/A (no official public code repository found; the paper provides reproducibility/hyperparameter details in the appendix but does not link a released code repo) [uncertain]
task_domain: In-context learning for few-shot semantic parsing / program synthesis (code-generation-like structured-output tasks). The method is framed as a general ICL exemplar-retrieval framework but instantiated and evaluated on semantic parsing.
problem_setting: Offline-trained, test-time-deployed exemplar retriever for in-context learning. Given a query and a fixed labeled training set D of (input, output) exemplars, the retriever must compose an ordered set of K=10 ICL exemplars to maximize the inference LLM's probability of producing the correct program. Single-agent (a retriever interacting with a frozen LLM treated as the environment). Supervision: reference target parses are available; the LLM provides token-likelihood feedback used as reward. Training is via RL (PPO) with the LLM as a simulator/environment; no human labels of exemplar quality are used.
what_is_retrieved: demos / ICL exemplars (input-output pairs, i.e. natural-language query paired with its target semantic-parse / program) drawn from the training set.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: retrieval targets the fixed labeled training set D (a static pool of exemplars). The store does not grow during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-oriented portfolio composition rather than fixed independent top-k ranking. The paper frames optimal exemplar-set selection as an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem (Eq. 1) and learns an approximation that models interactions among selected exemplars to build a 'portfolio'; however the final size is still a fixed K (k=10 in main experiments), so it is a fixed-size set whose composition (not just per-item similarity) is optimized.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning; only the Retrieve phase is present in a CBR sense - exemplars are reused verbatim as ICL demonstrations with no Revise/Retain).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as iterative retrieval / policy optimization (MDP/RL).
retrieval_unit: single demonstration (one ICL exemplar = a (query, target-parse) pair) retrieved per step; the full retrieved object is a fixed-length ordered sequence of K=10 such exemplars.
index_source: Static corpus: the retrievable store is the fixed training set D, built offline. Exemplar embeddings are precomputed and indexed (FAISS / maximum inner product search). No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index over exemplar encodings (Contriever/EPR embeddings) searched by maximum inner product search (MIPS) via FAISS. No graph or hierarchy.
retriever_type: Learned, stateful dense retriever: an off-the-shelf dense encoder (Contriever, optionally EPR-finetuned, frozen) augmented with a learned state-transition/policy module (GRU + query-projection Q + value head). Per-step retrieval is dense MIPS; the policy is RL-trained.
retriever_learning_signal: RL / learned policy trained with LM feedback. Specifically PPO (proximal policy optimization) with Generalized Advantage Estimation; the reward is derived from the inference LLM's completion probability of the reference output (the marginal increase in P_LM(y*|x; exemplars) contributed by each appended exemplar). This is downstream-task-effectiveness / LM-feedback signal rather than contrastive similarity labels.
query_construction: The query vector at each step is computed by a learned projection Q(s_i) of the current retrieval state s_i (a fixed-length state vector that summarizes previously selected exemplars). Initial state s_0 is a learned parameter; the state is updated by a GRU consuming the encoding of the just-retrieved exemplar. Thus the query is state-conditioned (history-aware) rather than a static encoding of the raw input.
query_granularity: step/state-level: a new query vector is constructed at each of the K retrieval steps, conditioned on the evolving retrieval state (the sequence of already-selected exemplars). Task-level input also seeds the process, but selection is iterative/step-conditioned.
when_to_retrieve: iterative: retrieval is performed in a fixed sequence of K steps (one exemplar appended per step) until K exemplars are assembled; it is not one-shot top-k, nor uncertainty-triggered/active.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: exactly one exemplar is retrieved per step for a predetermined number of steps (K=10 in main experiments). There is no learned/confidence-based trigger deciding whether to retrieve; the iteration count is fixed by the target exemplar budget.
reranking: No explicit separate reranking stage (no cross-encoder). Instead, the stateful policy implicitly re-scores candidates at each step via the state-conditioned query; during training a stratified sampling over the top-B buffer constructs the action distribution, but this is for exploration, not a reranking module at inference.
retrieved_context_refinement: none - retrieved exemplars are inserted into the prompt verbatim via a fixed template; no decomposition, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering is applied to retrieved content.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills retrieved; exemplars are raw (query, parse) pairs encoded by the text embedder).
index_content_separation: N/A - exemplars are both indexed (by embedding) and used directly as content; no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content separation.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: the ordered sequence of K retrieved exemplars is formatted into an ICL prompt via a predefined template and fed to the inference LLM for generation. During training, the same composition also produces the LM-likelihood reward signal that trains the retrieval policy. Exemplars are used as verbatim demonstrations (no adaptation).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate with iterative exemplar composition inside a learned policy/search loop: the iterative retriever builds the exemplar portfolio step-by-step (an MDP rollout) before the LLM produces the final output. It is not interleaved with the LLM's own reasoning steps; rather the LLM is used as the environment/simulator that scores partial exemplar sets during training. At inference, one full exemplar set is composed, then a single LLM generation produces the program.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer: retrieval (the K-step exemplar composition) happens before a single LLM answer generation; retrieval is not woven into per-CoT-step or per-token LLM reasoning. (The iterative steps are over exemplar selection, not over the LLM's reasoning.)
adaptation_mechanism: verbatim ICL exemplar - retrieved cases/exemplars are used as-is in the prompt; there is no LLM-prompted or feedback-driven revision of the retrieved exemplars themselves.
retrieved_item_representation: raw exemplar (a natural-language query plus its raw target semantic parse / program), injected as a verbatim ICL demonstration in the prompt; no distillation into strategy/guideline form.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: single demonstration (raw input-output exemplar). No abstraction into distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware/effectiveness-driven training: because the policy is trained with PPO using LM-likelihood reward, it learns to select exemplars that actually raise the probability of the correct output (and to avoid low-contribution exemplars), implicitly guarding against unhelpful retrievals; stratified sampling balances exploration vs exploitation during training. No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-filtering module.
memory_type: none - no episodic/skill/workflow memory is maintained; the only persistent store is the static training set. (The within-rollout 'state' vector is a transient MDP state, not a growing memory.)
write_back: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into a persistent memory at deployment. (During training, rollout trajectories are placed in a replay buffer for experience replay, but this is a training mechanism, not deployed memory write-back.)
online_growth: False - the retrievable store (training set D) is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow at test time.
write_back_trigger: never (at deployment). The retrievable exemplar store is fixed; nothing is written back during or after inference. (Training uses a transient replay buffer of rollouts only.)
failure_experience_usage: No persistent storage of failed experiences. During RL training, both high- and low-reward trajectories are sampled and used to estimate advantages (so negative/low-reward rollouts inform the policy update via PPO), but failures are not stored as retrievable corrective cases.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / none - no deployed memory to mutate (store is static; append-only replay buffer exists only during training and is not a persistent memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: True - case/exemplar selection IS a learned RL-optimized policy (MDP formulation; PPO with GAE; state-value head), explicitly contrasted against fixed similarity-based top-k retrieval.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No cross-agent sharing within a single run. However, the trained retriever generalizes across different inference LLMs (trained with Llama-2-7b but used with Llama-2-13b/70b, CodeLlama-70b-Instruct, and Mistral-7b), i.e. a degree of cross-model transfer of the learned retrieval policy.
benchmarks: SMCalFlow (Andreas et al., 2020), TreeDST (Cheng et al., 2020), and MTOP (English portion only; Li et al., 2021), following the BenchClamp benchmark (Roy et al., 2023).
benchmark_family: Semantic parsing / structured program synthesis (code-generation-like). Not in the standard QA/web/embodied/tool families; closest normalized grouping is 'semantic parsing / code-structured-output' under the ICL demonstration-retrieval setting.
baselines: BM25; Contriever (off-the-shelf dense retriever); EPR (Efficient Prompt Retrieval, Rubin et al. 2022, contrastively trained with scoring-LM labels; re-implemented with Contriever base for fair comparison); CEIL (Compositional Exemplars for In-context Learning, Ye et al. 2023, uses Determinantal Point Processes to model input-exemplar interaction). Non-iterative baselines are adapted by taking top-k with original ranks.
key_metrics: Exact Match at top-k (EM@1, EM@2, EM@3) reflecting beam-search decoding; and SMatch precision/recall/F1 (for the deeply-nested SMCalFlow and TreeDST, to credit correct substructures). All runs use k=10 exemplars, averaged over 3 inference runs; improvements over Contriever/EPR/CEIL are significant (paired t-test, p<0.05).
headline_result: IterR outperforms all baselines on all three datasets across all metrics. On SMCalFlow with Llama-2-7b: EM@1 = 54.1 (vs CEIL 51.1, EPR 48.5, Contriever 44.0) and SMatch-F = 77.3 (vs CEIL 75.1); on TreeDST EM@1 = 58.2 and SMatch-F = 85.7; on MTOP EM@1 = 63.9 / EM@3 = 71.0. Achieved by adding only ~4M parameters (110M -> 114M) to a frozen off-the-shelf dense retriever.
ablations: Table 2 (SMCalFlow, Llama-2-7b): (1) Removing EPR initialization (train from Contriever instead) drops EM@1 from 54.1 to 45.1 and SMatch-F from 77.3 to 68.8 - EPR init gives ~6% gain vs ~1% gain from RL alone, showing EPR domain-specific finetuning + restructured action space drives much of the gain. (2) Replacing GRU state transition with a Transformer decoder drops EM@1 to 50.1 / SMatch-F 75.1 and causes unstable training (warmup led to a trivial near-fixed trajectory). (3) Removing stratified sampling (sampling directly from buffer) drops EM@1 to 52.3 / SMatch-F 75.7, confirming stratified sampling's exploration benefit. Additional analyses: generalization across inference LLMs (Figure 5) and performance vs number of exemplars 1..10 (Figure 6, IterR matches baselines with fewer exemplars).
evaluation_decoupling: No - the paper reports only end-to-end downstream ICL task metrics (EM@k, SMatch) of the inference LLM. It does not report standalone intrinsic retrieval metrics (e.g. Recall@k/nDCG) decoupled from task performance.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-focused (final program EM and SMatch F1). SMatch adds partial-structure credit (substructure correctness), giving a finer-grained outcome signal; the number-of-exemplars analysis offers some process insight, but there is no separate step-wise retrieval-accuracy evaluation.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Parameter-efficient: only ~4M added parameters (110M->114M) atop a frozen retriever, with the encoder frozen. RL training incurs cost but is done once and ideally with a smaller LM (Llama-2-7b) then reused on larger LMs. IterR reaches comparable accuracy with fewer exemplars (Figure 6), enabling a performance-vs-cost trade-off that reduces LLM token consumption. No explicit latency/API-cost numbers are reported. [uncertain on exact wall-clock/training-cost figures]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: K=10 exemplars per prompt in the main experiments; selection-count analysis sweeps k in {1,...,10}. The k exemplars are composed sequentially by the policy (not reranked-then-truncated). No explicit token budget cap stated beyond the fixed exemplar count.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-construction paper; it uses existing SMCalFlow/TreeDST/MTOP datasets via BenchClamp). Dataset statistics are in Appendix A.1. [uncertain on exact per-split sizes used]
builds_on: EPR (Rubin et al., 2022, used as encoder initialization and baseline); Contriever (Izacard et al., 2022, base dense encoder); CEIL (Ye et al., 2023, DPP-based exemplar selection baseline); PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) and GAE (Schulman et al., 2016) for RL; policy-as-retrieval formulation similar to Lu et al. (2023); reward design inspired by Shin et al. (2021), Shi et al. (2023), and Zhang et al. (2022) (LM-likelihood / contribution-based reward); BenchClamp (Roy et al., 2023) evaluation protocol.
contrasts_with: Off-the-shelf single-call similarity retrievers (BM25, Contriever) that rank items independently by semantic similarity; contrastively-trained exemplar retrievers (EPR); and set-selection methods modeling interactions non-iteratively (CEIL/DPP). Key contrast: IterR is a stateful, iterative, RL-trained policy that conditions each selection on previously chosen exemplars and on LLM feedback, rather than a static top-k or one-shot set selector.
lineage: Group A: ICL demonstration retrieval. Positioned in the lineage of learned exemplar/demonstration retrieval for in-context learning (Contriever -> EPR -> CEIL), advancing it from one-shot similarity/set selection to a stateful iterative retrieval policy trained by RL with LLM feedback (a learned-policy / portfolio-composition view of demonstration retrieval).
